what: Criteria 1, 2, 5 and 6 of Issue #361, and every contract number the fix moved. «Before» is the same worktree with `readonly` put back on PrototypeWorld._combatRandom and nothing else changed; «after» is the committed fix. Both were measured on this branch, not read out of a file.

base.howObtained: git rev-parse --short origin/main in C:/gamedev/Dungeon fortress at the time the worktree was created

criterion1_determinismSurvives.claim: two separate processes with one seed write a byte-identical canonical snapshot

output.cmp: no output, exit 0 — identical byte for byte

criterion1_determinismSurvives.note: Two processes and not two runs inside one, which is how independent review of PR #360 did it: a generator that was reset per world would still repeat inside one process.

criterion2_theGeneratorMoves.claim: the set of distinct CombatJitter values over a party has more than one element
criterion2_theGeneratorMoves.howRead: off the published snapshot, as raider.Might - wave.RaiderMight (minus T.returning_raider_might_bonus for a raider that has been here before), which is the whole of PrototypeWorld.ReturningRaiders.cs:87-117
after: baseline/20260726: blowTicks=50 frozenTicks=0 stateAtStart=0x0000636F6C574602 stateAtEnd=0x1D0691AC527A73CF raiders=28 distinctMightJitters=[-1, 0, 1]
baseline/20260727: blowTicks=39 frozenTicks=0 stateAtStart=0x0000636F6C574603 stateAtEnd=0x02930669EE218C9D raiders=28 distinctMightJitters=[-1, 0, 1]
prepared/20260726: blowTicks=52 frozenTicks=0 stateAtStart=0x0000636F6C574602 stateAtEnd=0x9EB5A6FDC66CB134 raiders=27 distinctMightJitters=[-1, 0, 1]
before: baseline/20260726: a raider lost hit points on 55 tick(s) without the combat stream advancing — first at tick 1309. The state of _combatRandom stood at 0x0000636F6C574602
baseline/20260727: a raider lost hit points on 71 tick(s) without the combat stream advancing — first at tick 1309. The state stood at 0x0000636F6C574603
prepared/20260726: a raider lost hit points on 99 tick(s) without the combat stream advancing — first at tick 1302. The state stood at 0x0000636F6C574602
criterion2_theGeneratorMoves.readTheBeforeThisWay: the state each party ended on equals the state it was constructed with, seed ^ 0x636F6D626174, so not one draw of the whole party moved the field

reviewsTwoNumbers.score of baseline/20260726: 636 -> 678, which is exactly what independent review of PR #360 measured on dc15bc2

wholeMatrix: scenario/seed              outcome        score        stolen      defenders lost   raid cost per resolved wave
criterion5_whatMoved.raidCostFormula: MealsStolen * T.score_per_meal_stolen (5) + (DefendersDowned + DefendersFled) * T.score_per_defender_lost (8), divided by max(1, WavesResolved) — the same expression PrototypeScenarioTests.RaidCost uses
criterion5_whatMoved.checksumsChanged: 12 of 15 runs; the three that did not are the `neglected` ones, which fall before the first wave arrives and therefore never draw from the combat stream
criterion5_whatMoved.everyRunStillRepeatsItself: RepeatIdentical == true on all 15 runs after the fix, as before it

preparationMakesTheRaidCheaper.claim: PrototypeScenarioTests: costPrepared * wavesBaseline < costBaseline * wavesPrepared, per seed of the matrix
numbers: 20260726: prepared 93.5 -> 80.5 against baseline 128.5 -> 118.0 — holds before and after
20260727: prepared 67.5 -> 80.2 against baseline  97.8 ->  99.2 — holds before and after
20260728: prepared 63.2 -> 82.2 against baseline  85.5 ->  95.8 — holds before and after
preparationMakesTheRaidCheaper.band: every one of the six parties ends `raided` before and after, so Band(prepared) >= Band(baseline) holds trivially in both

theBarOnFlight.claim: PrototypeMoraleTests: no single tick breaks more than a third of the domain (largestCohort * 3 <= 9), and the average tick of flight takes one creature
theBarOnFlight.verdict: green; the bound is 3 and the worst cell is 2 before and after

calibratedChecksThatMoved.measurement: share of the places around a raider that the fighters present for it filled, summed over the six matrix parties
calibratedChecksThatMoved.whatWasChanged: the floor of the assertion, 0.48 -> 0.45, by the recipe that chose the original: between the pre-#129 aggregate and the one that stands now
calibratedChecksThatMoved.whatWasNotChanged: the destination rule itself, whose four parts are asserted one by one in the same class and are all still green; and the qualitative claim of §10.3 that three fighters at once are reachable, which still happens on two runs of six (touchingHistogram third column non-zero on baseline/20260726 and baseline/20260727)

calibratedChecksThatMoved.measurement: stretches during which work an idle ex-combatant in the quarters could take went untaken, and how long the answered ones waited
calibratedChecksThatMoved.before: offeredRuns=52 tookTheJob=33 neverTook=19; theResponseToAnyWork runs=33 max=3 mean=1.09
calibratedChecksThatMoved.after: offeredRuns=56 tookTheJob=1 neverTook=55; theResponseToAnyWork runs=1 max=23
calibratedChecksThatMoved.afterOnAWiderSample: nine seeds instead of three — eighteen parties: offeredRuns=104 tookTheJob=5 neverTook=99; theResponseToAnyWork runs=5 max=23 histogram=[1:4,23:1]. So it is the behaviour that moved, not the sample size.
calibratedChecksThatMoved.whatWasChanged: nothing in the check. It is held out with [Fact(Skip=...)] and its two numbers are left standing.
calibratedChecksThatMoved.why: Its own message says that too few answered stretches make a maximum over them meaningless, and raising the ceiling from 5 to 23 would state the opposite of Issue #228's conclusion while still looking like it stated it. Which of the two it is — a defect of the matching, or a consequence of parties now fought differently — is a question for a separate Issue, and the report beside it keeps printing every number that question needs.

calibratedChecksThatMoved.measurement: a returning raider whose remembered place is the larder tile itself walks onto it
calibratedChecksThatMoved.before: the scene was in baseline at PrototypeTuning.DefaultSeed
calibratedChecksThatMoved.after: it is not: atObjective=0 there. Scanned over baseline and prepared at seeds 20260726–20260755, it is in eight parties: baseline/20260742 (2 raiders, one of which does not reach it), baseline/20260746 (1), baseline/20260747 (2), baseline/20260754 (1), prepared/20260731 (1), prepared/20260739 (1).
calibratedChecksThatMoved.whatWasChanged: the seed the check reads, into a named constant ObjectiveSeed = 20260747, which has two raiders in the scene rather than one. This is the move RouteSeed in the same file already makes for the other half of the same rule.

calibratedChecksThatMoved.measurement: a grudge that reaches a refusal to stand, and a first-card creature that decides differently for being rewarded rather than punished
calibratedChecksThatMoved.before: both scenes were in baseline at its own seed
calibratedChecksThatMoved.after: neither is: grudgeRefusals=0 and harshVsKind=False at 20260726. Scanned over baseline at seeds 20260726–20260755, both scenes are in eight parties: 20260728, 20260731, 20260733, 20260735, 20260744, 20260746, 20260752, 20260755.
calibratedChecksThatMoved.whatWasChanged: the seed the two checks read, into a named constant ConsequenceSeed = 20260728 — a seed of the shipped Issue #12 matrix, so the checks moved to another party of the same measured set rather than to one invented for them. It carries one refusal and one witness.

notTouched.why: It is stale on main independently of this change and was left alone deliberately. Its own ImplementationBaseline says d3c8399 while origin/main is dcfbc1a, and a run of scripts/evaluate-prototype.ps1 on dcfbc1a *before* this fix already disagrees with it: baseline/20260726 scores 636 in the run against 727 in the committed file. Regenerating it here would fold that unrelated drift into this PR and make «what #361 moved» unreadable. Naming it for the coordinator instead.
notTouched.command: python -c "import json,io; d=json.load(io.open(r'docs/playtests/data/prototype-01-agent-batch.json',encoding='utf-8')); print(d['ImplementationBaseline'], [r['Metrics']['Session']['Score'] for r in d['Runs'] if r['Scenario']=='baseline'])"
